product.title: Why the Draft Isn't a Ranking
product.summary: Draft position reflects fit and need, not a pure ordering of talent.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students run a draft where the best available player is often the wrong pick, and work out how team need, position scarcity and cost change what 'best' means.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Runs end-to-end and is publicly reachable. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. The clearest decision-theory teaching in the account, and the only simulation that proves its own thesis rather than asserting it: a built-in Run 20 Drafts tool replays the identical strategy and returns a best of 93, an average of 64 and a worst of 40. Process Score and Outcome Score are reported separately.
knownBlockers: Positional need only loosely affects the Process Score — drafting three quarterbacks while other positions show HIGH need is barely penalised.

curation.tierBasis: The only simulation that proves its own thesis instead of asserting it: replaying one strategy twenty times returns scores from 40 to 93, and process and outcome are reported separately. The phone layout and keyboard access were repaired in this pass.
